-- Issue popcre/infrastructure#26
--
-- The consolidated DesignFlow non-production database inherited the seven
-- original Sample Tracking tables in `plm`, while the tracking service and all
-- later workflow objects use `dflow`. Move the existing objects; do not copy,
-- recreate, remap, or delete their rows.

BEGIN
SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '10s'
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '2min'
SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('popcre/infrastructure#26', 0))

CREATE TEMP TABLE issue_26_object_evidence (
  table_name text PRIMARY KEY,
  relation_oid oid NOT NULL,
  relation_file oid NOT NULL,
  row_count bigint NOT NULL
) ON COMMIT DROP

-- derived-from: 20260818024441
-- (dflow.validate_sample_path_revision() is re-derived in full from the body
--  last replaced by 20260818024441; that base must be present in the target.)
--
-- Issue #2136 -- dflow Sample Tracking: a sample a factory is asked to MAKE may
-- ship straight from the factory, to New York or to the customer, without
-- passing through Ningbo (owner-confirmed 2026-09-02).
--
-- Two widenings, and nothing else:
--   1. 'factory_customer' joins the allowed business_path value list on
--      dflow.sample_workflow and dflow.sample_path_revision.
--   2. workflow_type 'nyo_factory_make_request' may use 'factory_nyo' and
--      'factory_customer' in addition to 'factory_ningbo_nyo' and
--      'factory_ningbo_customer'.
--
-- The table CHECK dflow.sample_workflow.sample_workflow_valid_flow_path and the
-- BEFORE INSERT trigger function dflow.validate_sample_path_revision() are two
-- copies of one rule; both are widened identically here so a path revision can
-- never take a value the workflow table refuses, or the reverse.
--
-- The factory_to_customer route leg already exists
-- (20260724040000_sample_shipment_line_route_legs_explicit.sql) and is untouched.
-- Widening only permits more, so no existing row can violate the new rule and no
-- data migration is required. Constraint and function names are unchanged.
-- Re-applying this file is a no-op: every step is drop-and-recreate or
-- CREATE OR REPLACE against the same names.

BEGIN

-- Preconditions -------------------------------------------------------------
-- Everything is pinned to EXACTLY ONE object of exactly the right kind. A name
-- alone is not an identity: to_regclass matches a view or a matview, a pg_proc
-- match by name alone is satisfied by an overload while the real zero-argument
-- trigger function is missing, and a constraint name alone is satisfied by a
-- UNIQUE constraint. Each check below therefore counts, and refuses anything
-- other than one.
DO $$
DECLARE
  v_n integer;
BEGIN
  SELECT count(*) INTO v_n
  FROM pg_class t JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = t.relnamespace
  WHERE n.nspname = 'dflow' AND t.relname = 'sample_workflow' AND t.relkind = 'r';
  IF v_n <> 1 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Issue #2136 requires exactly one ordinary table dflow.sample_workflow, found %', v_n;
  END IF;

  SELECT count(*) INTO v_n
  FROM pg_class t JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = t.relnamespace
  WHERE n.nspname = 'dflow' AND t.relname = 'sample_path_revision' AND t.relkind = 'r';
  IF v_n <> 1 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Issue #2136 requires exactly one ordinary table dflow.sample_path_revision, found %', v_n;
  END IF;

  -- Pinned by SIGNATURE: zero arguments, returns trigger. An overload such as
  -- dflow.validate_sample_path_revision(integer) does not satisfy this.
  SELECT count(*) INTO v_n
  FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace
  WHERE n.nspname = 'dflow' AND p.proname = 'validate_sample_path_revision'
    AND p.pronargs = 0 AND p.prorettype = 'pg_catalog.trigger'::regtype;
  IF v_n <> 1 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION
      'Issue #2136 requires exactly one zero-argument trigger function dflow.validate_sample_path_revision(), found %', v_n;
  END IF;

  SELECT count(*) INTO v_n
  FROM pg_constraint c
  JOIN pg_class t ON t.oid = c.conrelid
  JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = t.relnamespace
  WHERE n.nspname = 'dflow' AND t.relname = 'sample_workflow'
    AND c.conname = 'sample_workflow_valid_flow_path' AND c.contype = 'c';
  IF v_n <> 1 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION
      'Issue #2136 requires exactly one CHECK constraint sample_workflow_valid_flow_path on dflow.sample_workflow, found %', v_n;
  END IF;
END $$

-- 1. Add factory_customer to the allowed business_path value list ------------
-- The two value-list CHECKs are column constraints, so their names were
-- generated by the server when 20260814130000 created the tables. Both names
-- are deterministic and are asserted here before anything is dropped, so the
-- names below are recreated exactly and this migration fails closed rather than
-- leaving a second, differently named constraint behind.
DO $$
DECLARE
  r          record;
  v_name     text;
  v_count    integer;
BEGIN
  FOR r IN SELECT * FROM (VALUES
      ('sample_workflow',      'sample_workflow_business_path_check'),
      ('sample_path_revision', 'sample_path_revision_business_path_check')
    ) AS expected(table_name, constraint_name)
  LOOP
    SELECT count(*), min(c.conname)
      INTO v_count, v_name
    FROM pg_constraint c
    JOIN pg_class t ON t.oid = c.conrelid
    JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = t.relnamespace
    JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = t.oid AND a.attname = 'business_path' AND a.attnum > 0
    WHERE n.nspname = 'dflow'
      AND t.relname = r.table_name
      AND c.contype = 'c'
      AND c.conkey = ARRAY[a.attnum];

    IF v_count <> 1 THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION
        'Issue #2136 expected exactly one business_path value CHECK on dflow.%, found %',
        r.table_name, v_count;
    END IF;
    IF v_name <> r.constraint_name THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION
        'Issue #2136 expected the business_path value CHECK on dflow.% to be named %, found %',
        r.table_name, r.constraint_name, v_name;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END $$

ALTER TABLE dflow.sample_workflow
  DROP CONSTRAINT sample_workflow_business_path_check

ALTER TABLE dflow.sample_workflow
  ADD CONSTRAINT sample_workflow_business_path_check CHECK (business_path IN (
    'factory_ningbo_nyo','factory_ningbo_customer','factory_nyo','factory_customer',
    'china_warehouse_ningbo_nyo','china_warehouse_ningbo_customer',
    'nyo_factory','nyo_ningbo','ningbo_nyo','ningbo_customer'
  ))

ALTER TABLE dflow.sample_path_revision
  DROP CONSTRAINT sample_path_revision_business_path_check

ALTER TABLE dflow.sample_path_revision
  ADD CONSTRAINT sample_path_revision_business_path_check CHECK (business_path IN (
    'factory_ningbo_nyo','factory_ningbo_customer','factory_nyo','factory_customer',
    'china_warehouse_ningbo_nyo','china_warehouse_ningbo_customer',
    'nyo_factory','nyo_ningbo','ningbo_nyo','ningbo_customer'
  ))

-- 2. Widen the nyo_factory_make_request arm of the flow/path matrix ----------
ALTER TABLE dflow.sample_workflow
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS sample_workflow_valid_flow_path

ALTER TABLE dflow.sample_workflow
  ADD CONSTRAINT sample_workflow_valid_flow_path CHECK (
    (workflow_type = 'nyo_purchased_factory_reference' AND business_path IN ('nyo_ningbo','nyo_factory')) OR
    (workflow_type = 'vendor_unsolicited_offer' AND business_path IN ('factory_ningbo_nyo','factory_nyo')) OR
    (workflow_type = 'nyo_factory_make_request' AND business_path IN (
      'factory_ningbo_nyo','factory_ningbo_customer','factory_nyo','factory_customer'
    )) OR
    (workflow_type = 'nyo_remote_china_inventory_request' AND business_path IN (
      'china_warehouse_ningbo_nyo','china_warehouse_ningbo_customer','ningbo_nyo','ningbo_customer'
    ))
  )
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION dflow.validate_sample_path_revision() FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated
COMMIT
